# Skill: Debugging a run

Read what the run already reports before you change a script or add a wait. Every signal below is
printed by `spectra run` (plain output, CI, or an agent's shell) and saved under `.testspectra/reports/`.

## 0. Agent workflow

```bash
spectra run <spec> --agent          # compact output; ends with a failure digest
spectra report                      # the same digest for the last run (--json for JSON)
```

For each failed case the digest gives `at:` (the spec/page-object line), `failed step:` (or
`after step:` when the test's own code threw), the error, the last steps, and three files:

- `page:` — `.testspectra/reports/snapshots/<case>.md`, a text outline of the page at the failure:
  URL, open dialogs, alerts, headings, every visible interactive element with its state
  (`disabled`, `covered by <div#overlay>`, `off-screen`) and a selector `Spectra.get()` accepts.
  Read it before the screenshot.
- `screenshot:` and `video:`.

The `⏱` line splits a case's time into setup / beforeEach / body / afterEach / artifacts and says how
much no step accounts for; `… untracked Nms` under a group is time spent outside reported steps.

### Breakpoints: look at the live page

```bash
spectra run <spec> --agent --break-at specs/Auth/TC-1/web.test.ts:42   # before the steps line 42 runs
spectra run <spec> --agent --break-at step:7                           # before step #7
spectra run <spec> --agent --break-on-failure                          # where it fails, before afterEach
```

Run it in the background; when it prints `⏸ Paused`, drive it from another shell:

```bash
spectra inspect                    # where it is paused and why
spectra inspect snapshot           # page outline with selectors
spectra inspect eval "document.querySelector('#email').value"
spectra inspect exec "await Spectra.get('~Close').click(); return Spectra.browser.getUrl()"
spectra inspect screenshot
spectra inspect next               # run one step, pause again
spectra inspect continue           # run to the next breakpoint or the end
spectra inspect abort              # fail the case here and stop the run (no hooks after it)
```

A breakpoint on an argument's line of a call written over several lines pauses at that call. One that never
paused (a blank or comment line, code that did not run) is named at the end of the run (`⚠ --break-at … never paused`).

Try a fix with `exec` on the paused page, then put it in the script. A pause nobody resumes continues
by itself after 15 minutes (`TESTSPECTRA_BREAK_TIMEOUT_MS`). Breakpoints run one worker and lift
the test timeout.

## 1. Signals and what they mean

| Signal                                                                                                                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                          | Do                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `── failure context ──` (`[TESTSPECTRA_FAILURE_CONTEXT]` as JSON)                                                     | The page when the test failed: the `Spectra.step` it failed in (`in step:`), last step, URL, focused element, open dialogs, input rates, CDP calls, a screenshot | Open the screenshot; check the focused element and the dialogs against what the step expected                                                            |
| `"resolved":"<button aria-label=…>"` on a click/type step                                                             | The element the action actually hit                                                                                                                              | If it is not the one you meant, the lookup is wrong (a position, a repeated name)                                                                        |
| `⚠ the page received N keydown events/s`                                                                              | Input is repeating (a stuck key, a script re-dispatching)                                                                                                        | Find the step named in the warning; the page is unusable after it                                                                                        |
| `⚠ the page's main thread is busy` / `CDP command … timed out during step #N`                                         | The page did not answer a command in 10 s; the rest of the message says what hangs (the next three rows)                                                         | Look for an input storm or long tasks first, not for a longer timeout                                                                                    |
| `… The page still answers: this command alone waited too long`                                                        | Nothing hangs: the command waited on a promise (a request, an animation)                                                                                         | Look at what the step waits for                                                                                                                          |
| `… The browser still answers but the page does not: this tab hangs`                                                   | The app froze the tab: a loop, heavy synchronous work, a huge render, memory running out                                                                         | Find the code the step triggered; the next test case gets a new tab and runs                                                                             |
| `… The browser did not answer either …: it hangs` / `[TestSpectra] The browser stopped answering: started a new one.` | The browser hung or crashed; the runner started a new one and ran the test cases that had no page again, once                                                    | The test case that was running keeps its failure; one still failing with `No browser page to run the test case in … The test case did not run` never ran |
| `[TESTSPECTRA_INTERCEPT] '<pattern>' (METHOD) answered METHOD <url>`                                                  | Which mock answered which request                                                                                                                                | A URL you did not mean: narrow the pattern (a glob matches the whole URL)                                                                                |
| `⚠ intercept '<pattern>' … answered no request`                                                                       | The mock never matched                                                                                                                                           | Check its URL and method                                                                                                                                 |
| `[TESTSPECTRA_STATE_CARRIED] … sessionStorage: <keys>`                                                                | Storage the previous test case left (`isolation: 'suite'`)                                                                                                       | A test that passes alone but fails in the suite: clear those keys in `beforeEach`, or set `webConfig.isolation: 'testcase'`                              |
| `⚠ another spectra run (pid …) is testing <url>`                                                                      | Two runs share one server and reset each other's data                                                                                                            | Stop one; results of both runs are unreliable                                                                                                            |
| `⚠ another spectra run (pid …) writes its report to <folder>`                                                         | Two runs share one report folder: the one ending last overwrites the other's report, snapshots and screenshots                                                   | Give each run its own `-o <own-dir>/result.json`                                                                                                         |
| `⚠ The machine has N MB of memory left; this run's processes hold M MB`                                               | The machine is short of memory: pages slow down, commands time out                                                                                               | Do not blame the app for a timeout after it: run fewer workers (`-c`) or close other programs, then run again                                            |
| `⚠ -c N starts more workers than the machine has room for now: K (…)`                                                 | The workers will compete for CPU or memory                                                                                                                       | Use `-c K` or fewer; the line names the cores and memory it counted                                                                                      |
| `Typed text did not reach … (focus was on …; the field is …)`                                                         | The keystrokes went elsewhere, or the field was disabled/inert                                                                                                   | Wait for the state that enables the field                                                                                                                |

**A case with several failures** (`spectra run --continue-on-step-failure`): `result.json` lists them
in `stepFailures`, in order, each with the `Spectra.step` it failed in, its message, `location` and a
screenshot and page outline of its own. `afterFailure: true` means another failure came before it:
read it first, it may only be a consequence (the earlier step left no state), neither drop it nor
count it as a new finding without looking. The case's own `failedStep` / `location` / `screenshot`
name the first failure. `stoppedBy: "maxConsecutiveStepFailures"` means the case ended at its limit
of failed steps in a row (`--max-consecutive-step-failures`): the steps after it were not checked.

`network-resources.json` holds every request with its HTTP method, request body and, when a mock
answered it, `interceptedBy`. The terminal no longer prints one line per request; set
`TESTSPECTRA_STREAM_NETWORK=1` to stream them.

## 2. A test that passes with `--delay`

It waits for no state. Ask the runner which step:

```bash
spectra diagnose --spec <id>
```

It reruns the spec with a wait after one step at a time, closest to the failure first, and prints
the step the test must wait after (`before step #33: click <button aria-label="Close dialog">`).
Put a `should*` assertion there for the state the app reaches — never a sleep. A global
`--delay` hides transient states a spec checks on purpose ("Checking availability…").

## 3. Probes, when the signals are not enough

```ts
await Spectra.browser.addInitScript(source); // runs in every document from its first instant
const stop = Spectra.onConsole(({ type, text }) => {
  /* … */
});
await Spectra.browser.cdp('Performance.getMetrics');
await Spectra.sleep(500); // probes only
```

Delete a probe spec when you are done.

# Skill: Suite & Global Lifecycle Hooks

Use this skill whenever you need setup/teardown logic (auth, DB seeding, cookie clearing, failure
screenshots) that shouldn't be duplicated inside every `it()` body.

---

## 1. Two Hook Levels — Know the Difference

| Hook                             | Level  | Scope              | When it runs                                                                                     |
| :------------------------------- | :----- | :----------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `global-hooks/before`            | Global | Entire run session | **Once**, before all suites — **Global Batch Run / CI only**, never during single-test debugging |
| `global-hooks/after`             | Global | Entire run session | **Once**, after all suites — Global Batch Run only                                               |
| `specs/<suite>/hooks/before`     | Suite  | Test suite         | Once before the first test case in the suite                                                     |
| `specs/<suite>/hooks/beforeEach` | Suite  | Test case          | Before every test case in the suite                                                              |
| `specs/<suite>/hooks/afterEach`  | Suite  | Test case          | After every test case in the suite                                                               |
| `specs/<suite>/hooks/after`      | Suite  | Test suite         | Once after the last test case in the suite                                                       |

**Global hooks are skipped when running/debugging a single test case** — put anything a single
test genuinely depends on (navigating to `/login`, clearing storage) in a **suite** hook instead,
not a global one, or the test will fail/behave differently when run in isolation.

Test cases of a batch share one browser session (`webConfig.isolation: 'suite'`, the default): what
a case leaves in cookies, localStorage or sessionStorage (a table's search and page) is there for the
next one, and the run prints `[TESTSPECTRA_STATE_CARRIED]` naming it. Reset that state in the
suite's `beforeEach`, or set `isolation: 'testcase'` when no `before` hook needs to log in once.

---

## 2. Directory Layout

```
workspace-root/
├── global-hooks/
│   ├── before/
│   │   ├── web.hook.ts
│   │   └── mobile.hook.ts
│   └── after/
│       ├── web.hook.ts
│       └── mobile.hook.ts
└── specs/
    └── authentication/
        ├── suite.md
        ├── hooks/
        │   ├── before/web.hook.ts
        │   ├── beforeEach/web.hook.ts   # e.g. clear cookies, navigate to /login
        │   ├── afterEach/web.hook.ts    # e.g. failure screenshot, clear storage
        │   └── after/web.hook.ts
        ├── TC-0001-valid-login/
        └── TC-0002-invalid-password/
```

---

## 3. Execution Order

### Single Test Case Run (VS Code CodeLens `▶ Run on <Target>`)

```
suite/hooks/before()
  └─► suite/hooks/beforeEach() ─► it('TC-0001') ─► suite/hooks/afterEach()
suite/hooks/after()
```

Global hooks do **not** run here.

### Global Batch Run (`▶ Global Run` / CI/CD)

```
global-hooks/before()                        (once, whole batch)
  ├─► Suite 1: before() → [beforeEach → TC → afterEach]* → after()
  ├─► Suite 2: before() → [beforeEach → TC → afterEach]* → after()
global-hooks/after()                         (once, whole batch)
```

---

## 4. Implementation: Anonymous Async Default Export

Same convention as steps/actions — one anonymous async function, default export, zero manual
imports:

```typescript
// specs/authentication/hooks/beforeEach/web.hook.ts
export default async function () {
  await Spectra.navigate('/auth/login');
  await Spectra.browser.clearLocalStorage();
  await Spectra.browser.clearCookies();
}
```

```typescript
// global-hooks/before/web.hook.ts
export default async function () {
  const response = await fetch(`${process.env.BASE_URL}/health`);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Target environment is not healthy: ${response.statusText}`);
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Failure Cascade Rules

1. **`beforeEach` fails** → that test case is marked `failed` (Hook Failure), its `it()` body is
   skipped, but `afterEach` still runs for cleanup.
2. **Suite `before` fails** → every test case in that suite is marked `failed` with the hook error
   and none of their bodies run (the reporter has no `skipped` state); suite `after` still runs to
   clean up partial resources.
3. **`afterEach` fails** → that test case is marked `failed` with the hook error, after its body ran.
4. **Suite `after` fails** → reported as a separate failed result titled `<last case> (after hook)`,
   so the run fails.
5. **`global-hooks/before` fails** → the entire batch run aborts immediately; `global-hooks/after`
   still runs to finalize cleanup.

Every hook failure prints a `TESTSPECTRA_TEST_ERROR` line naming the hook file and the error message.

Write hook bodies defensively with this cascade in mind — teardown logic in `after`/`afterEach`
must not assume `before`/`beforeEach` fully succeeded.

# Skill: Matchers, Actions & the Global `Spectra` API

Use this skill as the canonical vocabulary reference whenever you write the body of a test script
(`it()`), a shared step, or a custom action. TestSpectra never uses raw WebdriverIO/Jest matcher
names (`toBeDisplayed`, `setValue`, `$`) in authored code — always use the TestSpectra syntax below.
Every call is automatically traced (`trackCommand()`) and emitted as one natural-English log line
per action/assertion in `.testspectra/reports/`.

---

## 1. Element Action Commands (called on a Page Object getter)

| TestSpectra syntax                   | Semantic log output                     |
| :----------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------- |
| `await el.click()`                   | `Click on element "{el}"`               |
| `await el.doubleClick()`             | `Double-click on {el}`                  |
| `await el.rightClick()`              | `Right-click on {el}`                   |
| `await el.type(text, options?)`      | `Type "{text}" into element "{el}"`     |
| `await el.clear()`                   | `Clear text in {el}`                    |
| `await el.select(option)`            | `Select option "{option}" in {el}`      |
| `await el.hover()`                   | `Hover over {el}`                       |
| `await el.focus()`                   | `Focus {el}`                            |
| `await el.blur()`                    | `Blur {el}`                             |
| `await el.click({ x, y })`           | `Click on element "{el}" at (x, y)`     |
| `await source.dragDrop(dest)`        | `Drag {source} and drop onto {dest}`    |
| `await el.scrollIntoView()`          | `Scroll {el} into view`                 |
| `await el.longPress(durationMs)`     | `Long-press on {el} for {durationMs}ms` |
| `await el.waitForElement(timeoutMs)` | `Wait for {el} to be displayed`         |
| `await el.waitForElementRemoved(t?)` | `Wait for {el} to be removed`           |
| `await el.waitForUndisplayed(o?)`    | `Wait for {el} to be hidden`            |
| `await el.waitForClickable(o?)`      | `Wait for {el} to be clickable`         |
| `await el.getBounds()`               | `Get bounds of {el}`                    |

`type()` accepts an options object, e.g. `{ clearFirst: true }` to clear the field before typing.
`click({ x, y })` clicks at coordinates relative to the element; `Spectra.clickAt(x, y)` /
`Spectra.browser.clickAt(x, y)` clicks at absolute viewport coordinates.
`getText()` returns authored text (`textContent`) — CSS `text-transform` never leaks into assertions.
`getBounds()` returns `{ x, y, top, right, bottom, left, width, height }` (web
`getBoundingClientRect`, Android node bounds).

### 1b. DOM Traversal (cross-platform, no XPath)

| TestSpectra syntax           | Meaning                                               |
| :--------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------- |
| `el.parent()`                | Parent element in the DOM / a11y tree                 |
| `await el.closest(selector)` | Closest matching ancestor, or `null` (like `closest`) |
| `el.children(selector?)`     | Direct children as a collection (optional filter)     |
| `el.siblings(selector?)`     | Same-parent siblings (excluding self) as collection   |
| `el.next(selector?)`         | Next sibling, or first following sibling matching it  |

```typescript
await Spectra.get('ul').children('li').shouldHaveLength(3);
const card = await Spectra.get('#buy-button').closest('.product-card');
```

Collection index survives traversal: `getAll('.x').nth(1).parent()` resolves the second
`.x`'s parent, not the first document match. No XPath here by design — XPath dialects differ
per platform, traversal keeps one API.

### 1c. State Queries (return values, not assertions)

`await el.isClickable()` → `true` when visible + enabled + in viewport. Combines with
`isVisible()` / `isExisting()` / `isEnabled()` for explicit branching; prefer
`shouldBe*` matchers + `waitForClickable()` for plain waiting.

---

## 2. Element Assertions (called on a Page Object getter)

| TestSpectra syntax                        | Semantic log output                                      |
| :---------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------- |
| `await el.shouldBeVisible()`              | `Expect element "{el}" to be visible`                    |
| `await el.shouldNotBeVisible()`           | `Expect element "{el}" not to be visible`                |
| `await el.shouldExist()`                  | `Expect element "{el}" to exist in DOM`                  |
| `await el.shouldNotExist()`               | `Expect element "{el}" not to exist in DOM`              |
| `await el.shouldBeClickable()`            | `Expect element "{el}" to be clickable`                  |
| `await el.shouldNotBeClickable()`         | `Expect element "{el}" not to be clickable`              |
| `await el.shouldBeEnabled()`              | `Expect element "{el}" to be enabled`                    |
| `await el.shouldBeDisabled()`             | `Expect element "{el}" to be disabled`                   |
| `await el.shouldBeChecked()`              | `Expect element "{el}" to be checked`                    |
| `await el.shouldNotBeChecked()`           | `Expect element "{el}" not to be checked`                |
| `await el.shouldHaveText(text)`           | `Expect element "{el}" to have text "{text}"`            |
| `await el.shouldContainText(substr)`      | `Expect element "{el}" to contain text "{substr}"`       |
| `await el.shouldHaveValue(val)`           | `Expect element "{el}" to have value "{val}"`            |
| `await el.shouldHaveAttribute(attr, val)` | `Expect element "{el}" attribute "{attr}" to be "{val}"` |
| `await el.shouldBeFocused()`              | `Expect element "{el}" to be focused`                    |

Every assertion above (and every collection matcher in section 3) accepts a trailing
`options?: { timeoutMs }` to override the adaptive fail-fast timeout for that one call, without
raising it for every other assertion in the test — use this when a specific assertion is known to
need longer. To wait for an API, don't raise a timeout: `await spy.waitForResponse()` (or the
intercept handle's, after a deliberate `delayMs`) — see the `network-interception` skill.

```typescript
await ReportPage.statusBadge.shouldHaveText('Ready', { timeoutMs: 5000 });
```

**Whose failure** — `err.name` tells the app's verdict from the machine's: every `should*` throws `AssertionError`; a hung tab or browser, a closed tab, a device or run timeout throw `CdpTimeoutError`, `BrowserHungError`, `CdpSocketClosedError`, `DriverTimeoutError`, `CaseAbortedError` or `TimeoutError`. To collect several differences from a spec and fail with all of them at the end, catch only `AssertionError` and rethrow the rest (never `.catch(() => {})` around an assertion: that passes the case):

```typescript
const open: string[] = [];
const check = async (where: string, assertion: () => Promise<void>) => {
  try {
    await assertion();
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(err instanceof Error) || err.name !== 'AssertionError') throw err;
    open.push(`${where}: ${err.message}`);
  }
};
await check('amount', () => Page.amount.shouldHaveValue('10.50'));
if (open.length > 0) throw new Error(`${open.length} open gap(s):\n${open.join('\n')}`);
```

---

## 3. Collection Matchers (on `Spectra.getAll(selector)` getters)

| TestSpectra syntax                           | Semantic log output                                     |
| :------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------ |
| `await col.shouldHaveLength(n)`              | `Expect collection "{selector}" count to equal {n}`     |
| `await col.shouldNotHaveLength(n)`           | `Expect collection "{selector}" count not to equal {n}` |
| `await col.shouldHaveLengthGreaterThan(min)` | `count to be greater than {min}`                        |
| `await col.shouldHaveLengthLessThan(max)`    | `count to be less than {max}`                           |
| `await col.shouldBeEmpty()`                  | `Expect collection "{selector}" to be empty`            |
| `await col.shouldNotBeEmpty()`               | `Expect collection "{selector}" not to be empty`        |

---

## 4. Scoped Element Lookups: `.get()` / `.getAll()`

Any resolved element also has `.get(childSelector)` / `.getAll(childSelector)`, chaining a lookup
scoped to that element's own subtree — Playwright's `locator.locator()` model. **Prefer this over
a hand-written compound selector** whenever disambiguating repeated markup that shares one
selector across rows (a list of cards, a table's rows):

```typescript
// WRONG: `.buy-btn` is the same selector on every card — this always resolves the first one.
await Spectra.get('.buy-btn').click();

// RIGHT: scoped to the specific card first.
const thirdCard = Spectra.getAll('.product-card').nth(2);
await thirdCard.get('.buy-btn').click();
await thirdCard.getAll('.badge').shouldHaveLength(2);
```

Works identically from a Page Object property, since it's already a resolved element:
`await SettingsPage.modal.get('#save-btn').click()`. `.first()`/`.last()`/`.nth(i)` on a scoped
collection carry the scope forward too. No behavior difference on web vs. Android — resolution
(real DOM query vs. bounds-containment) is handled transparently underneath.

---

## 5. Global `Spectra.*` Commands

| Category       | Syntax                                                                                                                                                     |
| :------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Navigation     | `await Spectra.navigate("/login")` / `.back()` / `.forward()` / `.refresh()`                                                                               |
| Step group     | `await Spectra.step('TC-12: Sort by name', async () => { … })` — nests the actions under the spec's step title; returns `fn`'s value                       |
| Element query  | `Spectra.get(selector)` / `Spectra.getAll(selector)` — chain `.get()`/`.getAll()` on the result to scope a lookup, see section 4                           |
| Focus          | `await Spectra.focus(target)` / `await Spectra.blur(target)`                                                                                               |
| Coordinate     | `await Spectra.clickAt(x, y)` — absolute viewport click                                                                                                    |
| Window         | `await Spectra.setViewport(1920, 1080)`                                                                                                                    |
| Timing         | `await Spectra.wait(1000)`                                                                                                                                 |
| Keyboard       | `await Spectra.pressKey("Enter")`, chords `"Shift+Tab"`, `"ControlOrMeta+a"` (select all: Command on macOS, Control elsewhere); type text with `el.type()` |
| Scroll         | `await Spectra.scroll({ direction: "down", pixels: 400 })`                                                                                                 |
| Mobile gesture | `await Spectra.swipe({ direction: "left", distance: 300 })`                                                                                                |
| Network mock   | `const mock = await Spectra.intercept({ url, method, response })` — see the `network-interception` skill                                                   |
| Network spy    | `const api = await Spectra.spy(pattern, method); ...; await api.waitForResponse()` — see the `network-interception` skill                                  |

## 6. `Spectra.browser.*` — Browser/Context Level

| Syntax                                                             | Purpose                                                                                                       |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `await Spectra.browser.clickAt(x, y)`                              | Click at viewport coordinates                                                                                 |
| `await Spectra.browser.clearCookies()`                             | Clear all cookies                                                                                             |
| `await Spectra.browser.clearLocalStorage()`                        | Clear localStorage                                                                                            |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveUrl(url)`                         | Assert exact URL                                                                                              |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldContainUrl(substr)`                   | Assert URL contains substring                                                                                 |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveTitle(title)`                     | Assert exact document title                                                                                   |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldContainTitle(substr)`                 | Assert title contains substring                                                                               |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldBeLoaded()`                           | Assert page fully loaded                                                                                      |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveNoConsoleErrors()`                | Assert zero console errors                                                                                    |
| `await Spectra.browser.openTab(url?)`                              | Open a tab in the same session and act on it                                                                  |
| `await Spectra.browser.openTab(url?, { isolated: true })`          | Open a tab as a second browser: own cookies and storage                                                       |
| `await Spectra.browser.switchToTab(index)`                         | Act on tab `index` (0 = first; tabs the app opens follow in order)                                            |
| `await Spectra.browser.closeTab()`                                 | Close the active tab (any but the last), act on the one before                                                |
| `await Spectra.browser.openTab({ userAgent })`                     | Open a tab whose user agent is `userAgent` (also with `isolated`)                                             |

| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHavePageLoadCount(n, { tab? })`       | Assert a tab's load count: only the refreshed tab grew                                                        |
| `await Spectra.browser.waitForDownload({ timeout? })`              | Next file the page downloads: `{ fileName, path, size, text(), rows() }`                                      |
| `await file.shouldHaveRows(rows, { header? })`                     | Assert the CSV / first XLSX sheet; `header: false`: `rows` omit the header row                                |
| `await file.shouldContainRow(row)`                                 | Assert one row of the file equals `row`                                                                       |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveDownloaded(name \| /re/)`         | Assert a download with that name completed, polling                                                           |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldNotHaveDownloaded({ within? })`       | Assert no download this test case, nor in `within` ms (1000)                                                  |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveDownloadCount(n)`                 | Assert `n` downloads completed                                                                                |
| `await Spectra.browser.installClock()`                             | Fake page clock, before the page loads                                                                        |
| `await Spectra.browser.advanceClock(ms)`                           | Jump the clock; timers that fall due run                                                                      |
| `await Spectra.browser.answerDialogs({ beforeunload: 'dismiss' })` | Answer the case's next dialogs: `'dismiss'` is Cancel / Stay on page, `confirm: 'accept'` is OK, `promptText` |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveOpenedDialog(msg?)`               | Assert a JS dialog opened (each is answered as it opens)                                                      |
| `await Spectra.browser.shouldNotHaveOpenedDialog()`                | Assert none opened, nor opens for 500ms                                                                       |

Tabs, the clock, dialogs and downloads are web only, and reset when the next test case starts: one tab, no fake clock, no dialogs or downloads recorded. Install the clock before `Spectra.navigate`: timers the current document started earlier do not move.

---

## 7. Full Example

```typescript
it('should login as administrator and assert dashboard metrics', async () => {
  await Spectra.navigate('/auth/login');
  await Spectra.browser.clearCookies();

  await LoginPage.emailInput.type(Fixture.users.admin.email, { clearFirst: true });
  await LoginPage.passwordInput.type(Fixture.users.admin.password);
  await LoginPage.submitButton.click();

  await DashboardPage.header.shouldBeVisible();
  await DashboardPage.welcomeMsg.shouldHaveText('Welcome back, Admin');
  await DashboardPage.statCards.shouldHaveLength(4);
  await LoginPage.loadingSpinner.shouldNotBeVisible();

  await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveUrl('https://app.testspectra.dev/dashboard');
  await Spectra.browser.shouldHaveNoConsoleErrors();
});
```

This is engine-agnostic: the exact same syntax dispatches to Chrome CDP on `web.test.ts` and to the
native Android TCP driver on `android.test.ts` — never branch authoring code per platform inside a
shared file; instead put platform-specific implementations in the correctly-suffixed file (see the
`workspace-structure` skill).

description: How to write a TestSpectra Page Object (Spectra.get / Spectra.getAll singleton pattern) and how the ~accessibility-id vs #native-id selector contract resolves identically across Web, Android, and iOS. Use whenever declaring element locators or a new Page Object.

# Skill: Page Objects & the Selector Contract

Use this skill whenever you add a new Page Object, add a getter to an existing one, or need to
pick a selector string.

---

## 1. Page Object Pattern

A Page Object is a class with getter properties that return `Spectra.get(selector)` /
`Spectra.getAll(selector)`, exported as a singleton default export, and consumed with **zero
imports** anywhere else in the workspace (see the `workspace-structure` skill).

```typescript
// page-objects/MatchersPage/common.ts
class MatchersPage {
  get visibleElement() {
    return Spectra.get('#demo-visible-el');
  }
  get hiddenElement() {
    return Spectra.get('#demo-hidden-el');
  }
  get existingElement() {
    return Spectra.get('#demo-existing-el');
  }
  get productCards() {
    return Spectra.getAll('#demo-product-card');
  } // collection
}

export default new MatchersPage();
```

Rules:

- One getter per element/collection; name the getter for what the element _is_ (`submitButton`,
  `statCards`), not for the selector string.
- `Spectra.get(selector)` → single element; `Spectra.getAll(selector)` → collection (used with
  collection matchers like `.shouldHaveLength(n)`).
- Add reusable composite helpers as regular `async` methods on the same class, not as standalone
  actions, when they are specific to that one page.
- Page objects are platform-agnostic. Put a page object in `common.ts` when it uses only `~`/`#`
  selectors. Add `web.ts` / `mobile.ts` / `android.ts` / `ios.ts` only when a platform truly differs.
  When it differs and a `common.test.ts` uses it, add `expect.ts` beside them: the shape common
  scripts see (`declare const Login: { open(): Promise<void>; readonly emailField: … }; export default Login;`).
  Each platform file must match it (`tsc -b`); see `workspace-structure` § `expect` contracts.

### Nested page objects: `Page.*`

A folder holding a platform file is a page object. Folders above it are namespaces under one ambient root, `Page`:

| File                                            | Reference                                    |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------- |
| `page-objects/GsBrandListPage/web.ts`           | `GsBrandListPage` and `Page.GsBrandListPage` |
| `page-objects/GlobalSettings/Brand/List/web.ts` | `Page.GlobalSettings.Brand.List` only        |
| `page-objects/Shared/Toast/web.ts`              | `Page.Shared.Toast`                          |

- Use `Page.*` for any page object under a namespace folder. Flat page objects keep their bare global name.
- Do not name a page object `Page`, and do not give two entries the same name at one namespace level.
- `spectra refactor page-object GlobalSettings/Brand/List GlobalSettings/Brand/Detail` renames a nested page object and rewrites its `Page.*` references.

---

## 2. Selector Contract: `~name` vs `#name`

TestSpectra resolves selectors identically across every platform — a selector written once means
the same thing everywhere. Each prefix maps to **exactly one** attribute; there is no silent
cross-matching.

| Selector           | Meaning              | Web                   | Android                          | iOS                      |
| :----------------- | :------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------------- | :----------------------- |
| `~name`            | **accessibility id** | `[aria-label="name"]` | `content-desc`                   | accessibility identifier |
| `#name`            | **native id**        | CSS `#name`           | `resource-id`                    | — (n/a)                  |
| `name` (no prefix) | legacy lenient       | n/a                   | native id, then accessibility id | n/a                      |

### The contract

- Page objects select **only** by `~name` (accessible name) and `#name` (id).
- Never select by text content, class names, compound or structural CSS, or XPath.
- A repeated element or a table cell is reached by chaining `.get()` / `.getAll()` (or traversal)
  from its container. See section 3.
- Never write the unprefixed form (`name`). Always write `~` or `#`.

### Which one to use

- **Prefer `~name`** for anything a user can perceive.
- **Use `#name`** when the element has an id and no accessibility label (React Native `testID`,
  Android `resource-id`, CSS `id`).
- Set the _matching_ attribute on the app/page element so the selector actually resolves:

```tsx
// React Native — these resolve DIFFERENT selectors:
<Pressable accessibilityLabel="submit-button" />   // → Spectra.get('~submit-button')
<Pressable testID="submit-button" />                // → Spectra.get('#submit-button')
```

```html
<!-- Web -->
<button aria-label="submit-button">…</button>
<!-- → Spectra.get('~submit-button') -->
<button id="submit-button">…</button>
<!-- → Spectra.get('#submit-button') -->
```

- When `testID` and `accessibilityLabel` are set to the same value, `~name` and `#name` are
  interchangeable; they diverge the moment the two attributes differ.
- The unprefixed form (`name`) is Android-only leniency kept for backwards compatibility. It is not
  part of the cross-platform contract.
- Text content is not a selector. Give the element its own `~` or `#` attribute (`aria-label`,
  `id`, `accessibilityLabel`, `testID`).

---

## 3. Scoping a Lookup Instead of Writing a Compound Selector

When the same element repeats (a list of cards, a table's rows), **do not** write a compound or
structural selector (`#grid .buy`, `.card:nth-child(3) .buy`, `div > span`). Those are brittle and
have no cross-platform equivalent. Select the single container with `~`/`#`, then chain
`.get(childSelector)` / `.getAll(childSelector)` off it. The child selector is `~`/`#` and resolves
inside that container's subtree only. A `#` id is unique per page on web, so a repeated element is
reached through its container with a `~` name:

```typescript
class ProductsPage {
  get productGrid() {
    return Spectra.get('#products-grid');
  }
  buyButton(index: number) {
    return this.productGrid.getAll('~Buy').nth(index);
  }
}
```

Table cells follow the same rule. Select the table, then the repeated row or cell inside it:

```typescript
class OrdersPage {
  get ordersTable() {
    return Spectra.get('#orders-table');
  }
  orderStatus(row: number) {
    return this.ordersTable.getAll('~Order').nth(row).get('#order-status');
  }
}
```

This is a Page Object concern, not a new selector prefix. See the `matchers-and-assertions` skill
for the full `.get()`/`.getAll()` chaining behavior.

### Traversal instead of compound selectors

To move up or sideways in the tree, use traversal. It is the one cross-platform API for this.
Do not use XPath axes:

```typescript
class ProductCard {
  buyButton() {
    return Spectra.get('#buy-button');
  }
  async grid() {
    return this.buyButton().closest('#products-grid');
  }
  nextStep() {
    return Spectra.get('#step-1').next('#step-2');
  }
}
```

- `parent()` / `await closest(sel)` / `children(sel?)` / `siblings(sel?)` / `next(sel?)` work on
  web (DOM) and Android (a11y-tree links) identically.
- Index survives traversal: `cards.nth(1).parent()` resolves the second card's parent, never the
  first document match. Unfiltered `parent()` chains stay document-wide — scope with
  `closest(selector)` or a filter when several subtrees match.

---

## 4. Never Use Raw `$` / `$$` / `browser` / `driver`

TestSpectra encapsulates the entire runtime into a single global `Spectra` object. There is no raw
WebdriverIO `$`, `$$`, `browser`, or `driver` in test-authoring code — always go through
`Spectra.get()` / `Spectra.getAll()` for locators and `Spectra.*` / `Spectra.browser.*` for
everything else (navigation, gestures, storage, network). See the `matchers-and-assertions` skill
for the full command surface.

description: The difference between TestSpectra Shared Steps (Step.*, high-level business workflows, documented in spec.md via @step) and Spectra Actions (support/actions, low-level technical utilities) — directory layout, the mandatory anonymous async default export convention, and ambient type generation. Use whenever extracting reusable logic out of a test script.

# Skill: Shared Steps vs. Custom Actions

Use this skill when you're about to extract repeated logic (e.g. login, checkout) out of test
scripts, or when deciding whether new reusable logic belongs under `support/steps/` or
`support/actions/`.

---

## 1. Which One Do I Need?

| Attribute         | Shared Steps (`Step.*`)                        | Custom Actions (`Spectra.*` / on-element helpers)                             |
| :---------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Abstraction level | High-level business workflow (login, checkout) | Low-level technical utility                                                   |
| Directory         | `support/steps/<stepName>/`                    | `support/actions/<actionName>/`                                               |
| Spec mapping      | Documented as `@step:<name>` in `spec.md`      | Just called inline, not listed in spec steps                                  |
| Metadata file     | `step.md` (YAML frontmatter + description)     | None — implementation file only                                               |
| Files             | `step.md` + `web.step.ts` [+ `mobile.step.ts`] | `web.action.ts` [+ `mobile.action.ts`]                                        |
| Invocation        | `await Step.loginAsAdmin(params)`              | Called as a helper bound to an element/page, e.g. inside a Page Object method |

Rule of thumb: if it's a multi-step _business_ flow a human would describe in one sentence
("log in as admin"), it's a **Step**. If it's a small technical helper reused across Page Objects
(a resilient click retry, filling a pair of fields), it's an **Action**.

---

## 2. Directory Layout

```
support/
├── steps/
│   └── loginAsAdmin/
│       ├── step.md            # Metadata, docs, parameter types
│       ├── web.step.ts
│       └── mobile.step.ts     # optional
└── actions/
    └── fillCredentials/
        ├── web.action.ts
        └── mobile.action.ts
```

Both use **camelCase** directory/function names (`loginAsAdmin`, `fillCredentials`,
`applyDiscount`, `verifyOtp`) — never kebab-case or snake_case.

A step or action that is the same on every platform is one `common.step.ts` / `common.action.ts`
(an action that only calls a backend API is one). One that differs per platform but is called from a
`common.test.ts` gets a contract, `expect.step.ts` / `expect.action.ts`, beside its platform files:

```ts
// support/actions/shouldBeOnScreen/expect.action.ts — the shape a common script calls
declare const shouldBeOnScreen: (screen: string) => Promise<void>;
export default shouldBeOnScreen;
```

Each platform file is an actual with that signature (checked by `tsc -b`). See
`workspace-structure` § `expect` contracts.

---

## 3. `step.md` Metadata

```markdown
---
id: step-login-as-admin
name: loginAsAdmin
description: Authenticates as an administrator and asserts landing dashboard
platform:
  - web
  - mobile
tags:
  - auth
  - admin
parameters:
  - name: email
    type: string
    required: false
    description: Admin email address (defaults to Fixture.users.admin.email)
  - name: password
    type: string
    required: false
    description: Admin password (defaults to Fixture.users.admin.password)
---

# Login as Admin Step

## Purpose

Provides a standard, hardened administrative login sequence for web and mobile platforms.

## Prerequisites

- User fixture file exists at `fixtures/users.json`.
- Browser is navigated to the base URL or login route.
```

---

## 4. Implementation: Anonymous Async Default Export (Mandatory)

Every `*.step.ts` and `*.action.ts` file exports **one anonymous async function as its default
export** — no named exports, no `test()`/`it()` blocks. This is enforced by the linter
(`testspectra/require-anonymous-default-export`).

```typescript
// support/steps/loginAsAdmin/web.step.ts
export default async function (params?: { email?: string; password?: string }) {
  const email = params?.email ?? Fixture.users.admin.email;
  const password = params?.password ?? Fixture.users.admin.password;

  await Spectra.navigate('/auth/login');
  await LoginPage.emailInput.type(email, { clearFirst: true });
  await LoginPage.passwordInput.type(password);
  await LoginPage.submitButton.click();

  await DashboardPage.header.shouldBeVisible();
}
```

Custom Actions follow the same shape and are commonly written with a `this` receiver so they can
be attached/bound as element/page helpers:

```typescript
// support/actions/fillCredentials/web.action.ts
export default async function (this: any, email: string, token: string) {
  await this.get('#demo-email-input-pg').type(email);
  await this.get('#demo-token-input-pg').type(token);
}
```

```typescript
// support/actions/fillCredentials/mobile.action.ts
export default async function (this: any, email: string, token: string) {
  await this.get('~pg-email-input').type(email);
  await this.get('~pg-token-input').type(token);
}
```

Zero-import applies here too: never manually `import` a Page Object, `Fixture`, or `Spectra` — see
the `workspace-structure` skill.

---

## 5. Type Generation & Invocation

The `TypeGenerator` scans `support/steps/` and emits the `Step` ambient namespace automatically:

```typescript
declare global {
  namespace Step {
    function loginAsAdmin(params?: { email?: string; password?: string }): Promise<void>;
  }
}
```

### In `spec.md` (documents the step as part of the human-readable flow):

```markdown
## Test Steps

1. @step:loginAsAdmin
2. Navigate to user settings page
3. Update profile avatar
```

### In `web.test.ts` (invokes it with zero manual imports):

```typescript
it('should update admin profile avatar', async () => {
  await Step.loginAsAdmin();

  await SettingsPage.openProfile();
  await SettingsPage.avatarInput.type('avatar.png');
  await SettingsPage.successToast.shouldBeVisible();
});
```

Every `@step:<name>` in `spec.md` must have a matching `Step.<name>()` call in the paired test
script, or `spectra lint` reports `testspectra/missing-step-call`. See the
`spec-and-suite-authoring` skill for the full linter rule matrix.

---

## 6. Renaming a Step or Action

Never rename a step/action folder by hand. Use:

```
spectra refactor step loginAsAdmin authenticateAdmin
```

This atomically: renames `support/steps/loginAsAdmin/` → `support/steps/authenticateAdmin/`,
updates `name:` in `step.md`, rewrites every `@step:loginAsAdmin` in every `spec.md`, rewrites
every `Step.loginAsAdmin()` call site, and regenerates `.testspectra/types/steps.d.ts`.

Use this skill whenever you create a new test case, add a new suite, or edit an existing
`spec.md` / `*.test.ts` pair. TestSpectra treats the Markdown spec as the human-readable source of
truth and the TypeScript file as its execution — the CLI linter (`spectra lint`) enforces that the
two never drift apart.

---

## 1. Directory Convention

```
specs/<SuiteName>/suite.md
specs/<SuiteName>/hooks/{before,beforeEach,afterEach,after}/web.hook.ts
specs/<SuiteName>/TC-<NNNN>-<kebab-slug>/spec.md
specs/<SuiteName>/TC-<NNNN>-<kebab-slug>/web.test.ts   # + android/ios/mobile/common variants
```

`SuiteName` is a directory (no `describe()` block ever exists in code — the suite boundary is
purely the folder). Suites nest: `specs/GlobalSettings/Brand/suite.md` is a suite named `GlobalSettings/Brand`, and a test case belongs to the nearest ancestor folder holding `suite.md`. The test case id (`TC-0001-valid-login`) is both the directory name and the
`id` in `spec.md`'s frontmatter, and must be unique across the entire workspace
(`testspectra/duplicate-spec-id`).

---

## 2. `suite.md` Frontmatter

```markdown
---
name: Untitled Suite
id: suite-element-matchers
description: Element visibility, existence, form states and attributes
executionOrder: 1.0
parallel: true
---

# Suite: ElementMatchers
```

---

## 3. `spec.md` Frontmatter & Body

```markdown
---
id: TC-0003-visibility-and-dom
title: Verify element visibility and existence matchers
priority: High
caseType: Positive
status: ready-for-automation
coverage:
  web: automated
  mobile: automated
---

# Verify element visibility and existence matchers

## Test Steps

1. Open visibility section in matchers page
2. Assert visible element has be.visible state
3. Assert existing element exists in DOM
```

Required frontmatter: `id`, `title`, `priority`, `caseType`, `status` — missing any of these, or
missing the `# <Title>` / `## Test Steps` headings, triggers `testspectra/missing-frontmatter`.
Invalid enum values (an unrecognized `priority`, `caseType`, or `status`) trigger
`testspectra/invalid-frontmatter-enum`.

If the test case invokes a shared step (see the `shared-steps-and-actions` skill), reference it in
the `## Test Steps` list as `@step:<stepName>` — the linter cross-checks this against
`Step.<stepName>()` calls in the paired `*.test.ts`.

---

## 4. The Paired Test Script (`web.test.ts`)

```typescript
it('Verify element visibility and existence matchers', async () => {
  await MatchersPage.open('visibility');

  await MatchersPage.visibleElement.shouldBeVisible();
  await MatchersPage.hiddenElement.shouldNotBeVisible();

  await MatchersPage.existingElement.shouldExist();
  await Spectra.get('#demo-non-existent-el').shouldNotExist();
});
```

Each step the spec names (a `###` heading, or a numbered step that stands alone) is a
`Spectra.step` in the script, titled exactly as the spec names it. The run, the terminal, the
report and the VS Code panel nest that step's actions and assertions under the title, and a
failure names the step it failed in (`in step: TC-12: …`):

```typescript
it('Sort Brand Name, Used By (Items), dan Last Updated', async () => {
  await Spectra.step('TC-GS-BRAND-146: Sort Brand Name 3 state', async () => {
    await table.sortBy('Brand Name', 'asc');
    await table.shouldHaveCellText('Acme Corp', 'Brand Name', 0);
  });
});
```

A failed step ends the case by default. A run with `--continue-on-step-failure` goes on to the next
`Spectra.step` instead, and lists every failed step in `result.json` (`stepFailures`); the failed
step then returns `undefined`, so do not use the value of a step in a way that must not throw.

### Hard rules (each is a `spectra lint` error unless noted):

1. **Exactly one `it(...)` block, nothing else at the top level.** Zero or multiple `it()` blocks
   → `testspectra/single-it-required`.
2. **Never `test(...)`.** Only `it(...)` is allowed → `testspectra/no-test-block`.
3. **Never `describe(...)`.** Suite grouping is the directory, not code →
   `testspectra/no-describe-block`.
4. **Zero manual `import`s.** See the `workspace-structure` skill →
   `testspectra/no-manual-import`.
5. **`it()`'s title should read the same as `spec.md`'s `title`** (case-insensitive semantic
   match). A mismatch is a warning, not an error → `testspectra/title-mismatch`.
6. **Every `@step:<name>` in `spec.md` must have a matching `Step.<name>()` call** in the test
   script → `testspectra/missing-step-call` (error) if absent, and conversely a `Step.<name>()`
   call not documented with `@step:<name>` in `spec.md` is
   `testspectra/undocumented-step` (warning).

### Platform variants

A test case directory may contain any combination of `web.test.ts`, `android.test.ts`,
`ios.test.ts`, `mobile.test.ts`, `common.test.ts` — each is linted and can be run independently.
Reuse a shared step for the parts of the flow that are identical across platforms rather than
duplicating the `it()` body per platform.

---

## 5. Running the Linter

- `spectra lint` — scan the whole workspace, human-readable output.
- `spectra lint --strict` — treat warnings as errors, exit code `1` on any diagnostic (use this in
  CI).
- `spectra lint --json` — machine-readable diagnostics (what an AI agent should parse to
  self-correct after generating a spec).
- `spectra lint <path>` — scan a single suite or test case folder.

Exit codes: `0` valid, `1` violations found, `2` fatal (malformed YAML/JSON).

After authoring or editing a `spec.md`/`*.test.ts` pair, run `spectra lint <path-to-that-case>`
before considering the task done.

# Skill: TestSpectra Workspace Structure & Zero-Import Architecture

Use this skill whenever you scaffold a new TestSpectra workspace, add a new file to an existing
one, or need to decide where a Page Object / Step / Action / Hook / Fixture belongs.

---

## 1. Core Philosophy: Git-First, Spec-as-Code

Every test case, shared step, Page Object, fixture, and config file is a plain TypeScript or
Markdown file tracked in git — there is no proprietary binary project format. TestSpectra supports
two workspace paradigms:

1. **Default Project Mode** (`spectra init`, single-root repo) — one app, one `spectra.config.ts`.
2. **Monorepo / Nx Project Mode** (`spectra init --template nx`) — multiple `packages/*` test
   projects sharing a library under `shared/testing` (or a custom path), wired into
   `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

Never guess which mode a repo uses — check for `nx.json` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with a
`packages:` list first.

---

## 2. Default Workspace Directory Layout

```
my-test-project/
├── .testspectra/                # Auto-managed. NEVER hand-edit these files.
│   ├── tsconfig/                 # web.json, mobile.json, android.json, ios.json, common.json
│   ├── types/                    # web.d.ts, mobile.d.ts, android.d.ts, ios.d.ts, common.d.ts,
│   │                              # fixtures.d.ts — ambient globals (Spectra, Step, Fixture, POs)
│   └── reports/                  # report.json, network-resources.json, last-run.json
│
├── specs/                        # Test suites & test cases (Spec-as-Code)
│   └── <SuiteName>/
│       ├── suite.md              # Suite metadata (id, name, executionOrder, parallel)
│       ├── hooks/                 # Suite-level lifecycle hooks (before/beforeEach/afterEach/after)
│       └── TC-<NNNN>-<slug>/     # One directory per test case
│           ├── spec.md            # Frontmatter + "## Test Steps" with @step:<name> directives
│           ├── web.test.ts        # and/or android.test.ts / ios.test.ts / mobile.test.ts / common.test.ts
│
├── page-objects/                 # Page Object Model singletons
│   └── <PageName>/
│       ├── web.ts
│       └── mobile.ts             # (or android.ts / ios.ts)
│
├── support/
│   ├── steps/                    # High-level reusable business workflows (Step.*)
│   │   └── <stepName>/
│   │       ├── step.md
│   │       ├── web.step.ts
│   │       └── mobile.step.ts
│   └── actions/                  # Low-level technical utilities (Spectra.<action>())
│       └── <actionName>/
│           ├── web.action.ts
│           └── mobile.action.ts
│
├── fixtures/                     # JSON/CSV test data, auto-typed under Fixture.*
│   └── users.json
│
├── global-hooks/                 # Workspace-wide hooks, run once per Global Batch Run only
│   ├── before/
│   └── after/
│
├── spectra.config.ts             # Single source of truth for execution settings
├── tsconfig.json                 # References ./.testspectra/tsconfig.json — do not add "include"
└── package.json                  # Has "postinstall": "spectra sync-types"
```

For the Nx/monorepo variant, each `packages/<project>/` is its own self-contained workspace
(`specs/`, `page-objects/`, `spectra.config.ts`, `package.json`), and a shared library
(default `shared/testing/`) holds cross-project Page Objects/Steps/Actions/Fixtures. **Never** put
a `specs/` directory or a `spec.md`/`suite.md` file inside the shared library — the linter rejects
it (`testspectra/no-specs-in-shared-lib`).

---

## 3. Zero-Import Rule (Non-Negotiable)

TestSpectra scripts **never** contain a manual `import` statement for framework entities. Page
Objects, `Step.*`, `Fixture.*`, and the global `Spectra` object are all injected as ambient
globals via `.testspectra/types/*.d.ts`, which the CLI regenerates automatically (sub-60ms) when
you add/rename files under `page-objects/`, `support/`, or `fixtures/`.

- ❌ `import LoginPage from '../../page-objects/LoginPage';`
- ✅ Just reference `LoginPage` directly — it resolves globally.

Adding an `import` in a `*.test.ts`, `*.step.ts`, `*.action.ts`, `*.hook.ts`, or Page Object file
triggers linter rule `testspectra/no-manual-import` (error). If a file's types look stale after you
add a new Page Object/Step/Fixture, run `spectra sync-types` rather than importing manually.

---

## 4. Platform File Suffixes

| Suffix        | Target                      | Can access                                    |
| :------------ | :-------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------- |
| `*.web.*`     | Web (Chrome CDP)            | web + common                                  |
| `*.android.*` | Android (native TCP driver) | android + mobile + common                     |
| `*.ios.*`     | iOS (XCUITest)              | ios + mobile + common                         |
| `*.mobile.*`  | Shared Android & iOS        | mobile + common only (no web, no android/ios) |
| `*.common.*`  | Universal (web + mobile)    | common only (strictest isolation)             |

This applies to test scripts (`web.test.ts`), Page Objects (`web.ts`), steps (`web.step.ts`),
actions (`web.action.ts`), and hooks (`web.hook.ts`). A test that is not about one platform is
`common.test.ts`, so it runs on web and on mobile; `web.test.ts` is for what only the web has.

### `expect` contracts: one common script, an actual per platform

A common script may call an entity that each platform does differently (open a screen by URL on
web, by deep link on mobile). The entity's folder holds a contract, `expect.*`, and the actuals:

```
support/actions/shouldBeOnScreen/
├── expect.action.ts    # declare const shouldBeOnScreen: (screen: string) => Promise<void>;
│                       # export default shouldBeOnScreen;
├── web.action.ts       # export default async function (screen: string) { … URL … }
└── mobile.action.ts    # export default async function (screen: string) { … screen title … }
```

Steps use `expect.step.ts`, page objects `expect.ts`. A contract only declares its shape
(`declare const <name>: <type>; export default <name>;`, lint rule `testspectra/expect-contract`).

- **Types:** every platform takes the entity from its actual (`web` → `web.*`, then `common.*`),
  else from `expect.*`, since each platform's program also compiles the common scripts. Each actual
  is checked against the contract in `.testspectra/types/<platform>.actuals.ts`, so a wrong
  signature fails `tsc -b`.
- **Run:** the run's platform loads its actual (`web` → `web`, then `common`). With no actual for that
  platform, calling the entity fails with what to add (`… has a contract (expect.action.ts) but no
actual for platform "android": add android.action.ts (or the common one) in …`). The contract file
  is never loaded.
- An entity that is the same everywhere has no contract: one `common.*` file.

**Split at the smallest unit.** When a page object, step or flow is the same on every platform but
one step, keep it one `common.*` file and put only that step behind a contract. Name the contract
for what the step achieves, not how one platform does it (`passBotCheck`, not `solveRecaptcha`);
a platform where the step does not exist gets an actual that does nothing. Never copy a whole page
object or script per platform for one differing step. A script stays `web.test.ts` (or
`mobile.test.ts`) only when its subject is a mechanism that one platform has (a captcha's caption,
a browser tab), not when it merely passes through one.

---

## 5. `spectra.config.ts`

```typescript
import { defineConfig } from '@testspectra/cli';

export default defineConfig({
  webConfig: {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:5173',
    maxConcurrentSessions: '1',
    headless: true,
    implicitWait: '5000',
    parallelizationMode: 'testcase', // "testcase" | "suite"
    isolation: 'suite', // "suite": cases share the browser session (a before hook logs in once) | "testcase": empty cookies and storage per case
    viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }, // the page size every case starts at (the default); a case's Spectra.setViewport() does not leak into the next
  },
  androidConfig: {
    driverServer: 'tcp://127.0.0.1:8200',
    appPackage: 'dev.example.app',
    appActivity: 'dev.example.app.MainActivity',
    noReset: false,
    implicitWait: '10000',
    parallelizationMode: 'suite',
    devices: [{ id: 'emulator-5554', name: 'Pixel 8a Emulator', version: '14.0', systemPort: 8200 }],
  },
  iosConfig: {
    appiumServer: 'http://127.0.0.1:4723',
    automationName: 'XCUITest',
    bundleId: '',
    autoAcceptAlerts: true,
    noReset: false,
    implicitWait: '10000',
    parallelizationMode: 'suite',
    devices: [
      { id: 'iphone-15-pro', name: 'iPhone 15 Pro Simulator', version: '17.0', udid: 'auto', wdaLocalPort: 8100 },
    ],
  },
  executionConfig: {
    networkMonitoringEnabled: true,
    fastResponseTime: '200',
    normalResponseTime: '1000',
    monitoredDomains: [{ domain: 'api.example.com', enabled: true }],
    environmentVariables: { API_MODE: 'sandbox' },
    plugins: ['@myorg/spectra-button-plugin'],
  },
});
```

Numeric-looking fields (timeouts, ports, session counts) accept either a `number` or a numeric
`string` — stay consistent with whatever the rest of the file already uses.

`executionConfig` notes:

- **`monitoredDomains`**: empty/absent = record every domain; non-empty = only requests matching
  an `enabled: true` entry (exact hostname or leading-`*` wildcard) get recorded/streamed to the
  Network panel. `networkMonitoringEnabled: false` disables recording outright regardless of this
  list.
- **`fastResponseTime`/`normalResponseTime`**: millisecond thresholds the VS Code Network panel
  uses to color each request's Duration cell (fast/normal/slow). No effect on test execution
  itself.
- **`environmentVariables`**: a flat `Record<string, string>` (not an array, not nested
  key/value pairs) — every key becomes both a typed `Spectra.env.KEY` entry (generated into
  `.testspectra/types/env.d.ts`, autocompleted, zero-import — **prefer this over `process.env`**,
  which is untyped `string | undefined`) and a plain `process.env.KEY` string for code that must
  consume the untyped standard API.
- **`plugins`**: module specifiers (package name or project-relative path) extending `Spectra`
  with custom commands via `Spectra.registerCommand()`; installs are idempotent per specifier.
  Run `spectra sync-types` to regenerate per-platform ambient declarations.

## 6. Core `spectra` CLI Commands

| Command                                              | Purpose                                                                                                 |
| :--------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `spectra init [--template nx]`                       | Scaffold a new workspace                                                                                |
| `spectra sync-types`                                 | Regenerate `.testspectra/types` and `.testspectra/tsconfig` (also runs on `postinstall` and file-watch) |
| `spectra run [path] -t <web\|mobile\|android\|ios>`  | Execute tests                                                                                           |
| `spectra lint [path] [--strict] [--json]`            | Validate `spec.md`/`suite.md` schema + code parity (see the `spec-and-suite-authoring` skill)           |
| `spectra doctor`                                     | Preflight dependency/environment health check                                                           |
| `spectra refactor step\|action\|fixture <old> <new>` | Atomically rename across folder, metadata, and all call sites                                           |
| `spectra watch`                                      | Background file watcher driving `sync-types`                                                            |

After scaffolding or renaming any file under `page-objects/`, `support/`, or `fixtures/`, assume
the ambient types are stale until `sync-types` (or the watcher) has run — don't hand-write
`.testspectra/types/*.d.ts` yourself.

# @testspectra/skills

Modular AI agent skills installer & manager for standardizing **TestSpectra** script authoring —
specs, Page Objects, shared steps, custom actions, lifecycle hooks, fixtures, and the matcher
vocabulary.

Distributed the same way as [`@testspectra/matchers`](../matchers): as a standalone npm package
with its own CLI, installable independently of the main `@testspectra/cli`. When `@testspectra/cli`
is already installed in a workspace, the exact same commands are also available unified under
`spectra skills` — no separate install required.

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. One-time setup: pick agent(s) + which skills to install, in one guided flow
npx @testspectra/skills init          # or: spectra skills init

# 2. Standalone binary (works with zero other TestSpectra packages installed)
npx @testspectra/skills list
npx @testspectra/skills add
npx @testspectra/skills add workspace-structure spec-and-suite-authoring matchers-and-assertions
npx @testspectra/skills update
npx @testspectra/skills remove network-interception

# Unified under the main CLI (equivalent — use whichever is already installed)
spectra skills list
spectra skills add
spectra skills add workspace-structure spec-and-suite-authoring matchers-and-assertions
spectra skills update
spectra skills remove network-interception
```

`init` is a two-step guided flow:

1. **Pick agent(s)** — which AI agent(s) the project uses (Claude Code, OpenCode, Kilo, Universal
   `.agents`, or the global Gemini CLI). Saved to `.spectra-skills.json` at the workspace root, so
   every later `list`/`add`/`update`/`remove` call reads it automatically — no need to re-detect or
   re-specify agents each time. Without `init`, commands fall back to auto-detecting only agent
   directories that already exist in the target workspace.
2. **Pick skills** — a multiselect (all 8 pre-checked) of which skills to install right away for
   the agent(s) just selected. Deselect what you don't want, or submit empty to skip installing
   anything yet (you can always run `add` later).

A one-off `--agent <ids>` (or `-a` on `spectra skills`) flag on `list`/`add`/`update`/`remove`
overrides the saved selection for a single invocation.

---

## Available Skills

| Skill                        | Covers                                                                                            |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `workspace-structure`        | Directory layout, zero-import architecture, file suffixes, `spectra.config.ts`, core CLI commands |
| `debugging-runs`             | Reading a failing or slow run: failure context, warnings, intercept records, `spectra diagnose`   |
| `spec-and-suite-authoring`   | `suite.md` / `spec.md` frontmatter, the paired `*.test.ts` script, every `spectra lint` rule      |
| `page-objects-and-selectors` | Page Object pattern (`Spectra.get`/`getAll`), the `~`/`#` selector contract                       |
| `matchers-and-assertions`    | Full element action/assertion/collection matcher and global `Spectra.*` command reference         |
| `shared-steps-and-actions`   | `Step.*` business workflows vs `support/actions/*` technical utilities                            |
| `lifecycle-hooks`            | `global-hooks/` vs `specs/<suite>/hooks/`, execution order, failure cascade                       |
| `fixtures-data`              | `fixtures/*.json` and the ambient `Fixture.*` namespace                                           |
| `network-interception`       | `Spectra.intercept()` mocking and failure simulation; `Spectra.spy()` to wait for a real API      |

Each skill is grounded in `docs/v2/` and the reference workspace at `cli/templates/default`, so an
AI coding agent scaffolding TestSpectra scripts produces code that already passes `spectra lint`.

---

## Features

- **Multi-Agent, Cross-Platform**: Installs into `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`,
  `.opencode/skills`, `.kilo/skills`, and the Gemini CLI's global skills directory. `init` lets you
  pick explicitly; otherwise it auto-detects whichever the target project/agent already uses.
- **Independent Usage**: Works in any TestSpectra workspace (default or Nx/monorepo template)
  without requiring the main `@testspectra/cli` to be installed first.
- **Update-in-Place**: `update` re-installs every currently-installed skill from the package's
  current registry, so bumping `@testspectra/skills` and re-running `update` refreshes local
  copies.
